name: Laos
summary: Red, blue and red horizontal bands, the blue twice as tall, with a white disc in the centre. Used by the Lao Issara and Pathet Lao movements, it became the national flag when the communist Lao People's Democratic Republic was declared in 1975.
origin: The flag was first used by the Lao Issara nationalist government in 1945, and later by the communist Pathet Lao. The Kingdom of Laos (1949–1975) used a red flag with a three-headed white elephant under a parasol.
When the monarchy was abolished on 2 December 1975, the Pathet Lao flag became the national flag.

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: The wealth of the country; also the Mekong River.

symbols.name: White disc
symbols.description: A circle centred in the blue band.
symbols.meaning: The full moon over the Mekong; also the unity of the people under the government.

facts: It is one of the few communist-state flags without a star or a hammer and sickle.
The royal flag's three-headed elephant is Erawan, mount of the god Indra.
Its disc is often described as the moon rising over the Mekong.
clues: Red, double-height blue and red bands with a white disc in the centre.
Its disc is the full moon over a great river.
It replaced a flag showing a three-headed elephant in 1975.
